```
1	(shell-completion)=
2	
3	# Shell Completion
4	
5	```{currentmodule} click.shell_completion
6	```
7	
8	Click provides tab completion support for Bash (version 4.4 and up), Zsh, and Fish. It is possible to add support for
9	other shells too, and suggestions can be customized at multiple levels.
10	
11	Shell completion suggests command names, option names, and values for choice, file, and path parameter types. Options
12	are only listed if at least a dash has been entered. Hidden commands and options are not shown.
13	
14	```console
15	$ repo <TAB><TAB>
16	clone  commit  copy  delete  setuser
17	$ repo clone -<TAB><TAB>
18	--deep  --help  --rev  --shallow  -r
19	```
20	
21	## Enabling Completion
22	
23	Completion is only available if a script is installed and invoked through an entry point, not through the `python`
24	command. See {doc}`entry-points`. Once the executable is installed, calling it with a special environment variable will
25	put Click in completion mode.
26	
27	To enable shell completion, the user needs to register a special function with their shell. The exact script varies
28	depending on the shell you are using. Click will output it when called with `_{FOO_BAR}_COMPLETE` set to
29	`{shell}_source`. `{FOO_BAR}` is the executable name in uppercase with dashes replaced by underscores. It is
30	conventional but not strictly required for environment variable names to be in upper case. This convention helps
31	distinguish environment variables from regular shell variables and commands, making scripts and configuration files more
32	readable and easier to maintain. The built-in shells are `bash`, `zsh`, and `fish`.
33	
34	Provide your users with the following instructions customized to your program name. This uses `foo-bar` as an example.
35	
36	```{eval-rst}
37	.. tabs::
38	
39	    .. group-tab:: Bash
40	
41	        Add this to ``~/.bashrc``:
42	
43	        .. code-block:: bash
44	
45	            eval "$(_FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=bash_source foo-bar)"
46	
47	    .. group-tab:: Zsh
48	
49	        Add this to ``~/.zshrc``:
50	
51	        .. code-block:: zsh
52	
53	            eval "$(_FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=zsh_source foo-bar)"
54	
55	    .. group-tab:: Fish
56	
57	        Add this to ``~/.config/fish/completions/foo-bar.fish``:
58	
59	        .. code-block:: fish
60	
61	            _FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=fish_source foo-bar | source
62	
63	        This is the same file used for the activation script method
64	        below. For Fish it's probably always easier to use that method.
65	```
66	
67	Using `eval` means that the command is invoked and evaluated every time a shell is started, which can delay shell
68	responsiveness. To speed it up, write the generated script to a file, then source that. You can generate the files ahead
69	of time and distribute them with your program to save your users a step.
70	
71	```{eval-rst}
72	.. tabs::
73	
74	    .. group-tab:: Bash
75	
76	        Save the script somewhere.
77	
78	        .. code-block:: bash
79	
80	            _FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=bash_source foo-bar > ~/.foo-bar-complete.bash
81	
82	        Source the file in ``~/.bashrc``.
83	
84	        .. code-block:: bash
85	
86	            . ~/.foo-bar-complete.bash
87	
88	    .. group-tab:: Zsh
89	
90	        Save the script somewhere.
91	
92	        .. code-block:: bash
93	
94	            _FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=zsh_source foo-bar > ~/.foo-bar-complete.zsh
95	
96	        Source the file in ``~/.zshrc``.
97	
98	        .. code-block:: bash
99	
100	            . ~/.foo-bar-complete.zsh
101	
102	    .. group-tab:: Fish
103	
104	        Save the script to ``~/.config/fish/completions/foo-bar.fish``:
105	
106	        .. code-block:: fish
107	
108	            _FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=fish_source foo-bar > ~/.config/fish/completions/foo-bar.fish
109	```
110	
111	After modifying the shell config, you need to start a new shell in order for the changes to be loaded.
112	
113	## Custom Type Completion
114	
115	When creating a custom {class}`~click.ParamType`, override its {meth}`~click.ParamType.shell_complete` method to provide
116	shell completion for parameters with the type. The method must return a list of {class}`~CompletionItem` objects.
117	Besides the value, these objects hold metadata that shell support might use. The built-in implementations use `type` to
118	indicate special handling for paths, and `help` for shells that support showing a help string next to a suggestion.
119	
120	In this example, the type will suggest environment variables that start with the incomplete value.
121	
122	```python
123	class EnvVarType(ParamType[str]):
124	    name = "envvar"
125	
126	    def shell_complete(self, ctx, param, incomplete):
127	        return [
128	            CompletionItem(name)
129	            for name in os.environ if name.startswith(incomplete)
130	        ]
131	
132	@click.command()
133	@click.option("--ev", type=EnvVarType())
134	def cli(ev):
135	    click.echo(os.environ[ev])
136	```
137	
138	## Overriding Value Completion
139	
140	Value completions for a parameter can be customized without a custom type by providing a `shell_complete` function. The
141	function is used instead of any completion provided by the type. It is passed 3 positional arguments:
142	
143	- `ctx` - The current command context.
144	- `param` - The current parameter requesting completion.
145	- `incomplete` - The partial word that is being completed. May be an empty string if no characters have been entered
146	  yet.
147	
148	It must return a list of {class}`CompletionItem` objects, or as a shortcut it can return a list of strings.
149	
150	In this example, the command will suggest environment variables that start with the incomplete value.
151	
152	```python
153	def complete_env_vars(ctx, param, incomplete):
154	    return [k for k in os.environ if k.startswith(incomplete)]
155	
156	@click.command()
157	@click.argument("name", shell_complete=complete_env_vars)
158	def cli(name):
159	    click.echo(f"Name: {name}")
160	    click.echo(f"Value: {os.environ[name]}")
161	```
162	
163	## Adding Support for a Shell
164	
165	Support can be added for shells that do not come built in. Be sure to check PyPI to see if there's already a package
166	that adds support for your shell. This topic is very technical, you'll want to look at Click's source to study the
167	built-in implementations.
168	
169	Shell support is provided by subclasses of {class}`ShellComplete` registered with {func}`add_completion_class`. When
170	Click is invoked in completion mode, it calls {meth}`~ShellComplete.source` to output the completion script, or
171	{meth}`~ShellComplete.complete` to output completions. The base class provides default implementations that require
172	implementing some smaller parts.
173	
174	First, you'll need to figure out how your shell's completion system works and write a script to integrate it with Click.
175	It must invoke your program with the environment variable `_{FOO_BAR}_COMPLETE` set to `{shell}_complete` and pass the
176	complete args and incomplete value. How it passes those values, and the format of the completion response from Click is
177	up to you.
178	
179	In your subclass, set {attr}`ShellComplete.source_template` to the completion script. The default implementation will
180	perform `%` formatting with the following variables:
181	
182	- `complete_func` - A safe name for the completion function defined in the script.
183	- `complete_var` - The environment variable name for passing the `{shell}_complete` instruction.
184	- `foo_bar` - The name of the executable being completed.
185	
186	The example code is for a made up shell "My Shell" or "mysh" for short.
187	
188	```python
189	from click.shell_completion import add_completion_class
190	from click.shell_completion import ShellComplete
191	
192	_mysh_source = """\
193	%(complete_func)s {
194	    response=$(%(complete_var)s=mysh_complete %(foo_bar)s)
195	    # parse response and set completions somehow
196	}
197	call-on-complete %(foo_bar)s %(complete_func)s
198	"""
199	
200	@add_completion_class
201	class MyshComplete(ShellComplete):
202	    name = "mysh"
203	    source_template = _mysh_source
204	```
205	
206	Next, implement {meth}`~ShellComplete.get_completion_args`. This must get, parse, and return the complete args and
207	incomplete value from the completion script. For example, for the Bash implementation the `COMP_WORDS` env var contains
208	the command line args as a string, and the `COMP_CWORD` env var contains the index of the incomplete arg. The method
209	must return a `(args, incomplete)` tuple.
210	
211	```python
212	import os
213	from click.parser import split_arg_string
214	
215	class MyshComplete(ShellComplete):
216	    ...
217	
218	    def get_completion_args(self):
219	        args = split_arg_string(os.environ["COMP_WORDS"])
220	
221	        if os.environ["COMP_PARTIAL"] == "1":
222	            incomplete = args.pop()
223	            return args, incomplete
224	
225	        return args, ""
226	```
227	
228	Finally, implement {meth}`~ShellComplete.format_completion`. This is called to format each {class}`CompletionItem` into a string. For example, the Bash implementation returns `f"{item.type},{item.value}` (it doesn't support help strings), and the Zsh implementation returns each part separated by a newline, replacing empty help with a `_` placeholder. This format is entirely up to what you parse with your completion script.
229	
230	The `type` value is usually `plain`, but it can be another value that the completion script can switch on. For example,
231	`file` or `dir` can tell the shell to handle path completion, since the shell is better at that than Click.
232	
233	```python
234	class MyshComplete(ShellComplete):
235	    ...
236	
237	    def format_completion(self, item):
238	        return f"{item.type}\t{item.value}"
239	```
240	
241	With those three things implemented, the new shell support is ready. In case those weren't sufficient, there are more
242	parts that can be overridden, but that probably isn't necessary.
243	
244	The activation instructions will again depend on how your shell works. Use the following to generate the completion
245	script, then load it into the shell somehow.
246	
247	```console
248	_FOO_BAR_COMPLETE=mysh_source foo-bar
249	```
```
